strengths: Clear practical motivation for reusing computational investment in intermediate checkpoints with systematic framework
Comprehensive and thorough experimental validation including timing analysis across 12 checkpoints and large-scale 70B model experiments

Well-justified design choices with empirical evidence: layer-wise norm distributions observed across multiple open-source models supporting interpositional method; noise injection shows measurable improvement
Excellent reproducibility with extensive implementation details (Appendix D), complete evaluation tables (Appendix E), and promised code release
Actionable practical insights including heuristics for FLOPs allocation and guidance on depth vs. width growth trade-offs
Compelling empirical findings showing positive correlation between sunk cost and final performance
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: model growth is well-established; interpositional method is straightforward variant of existing approaches; noise injection for MoE relates to prior work; primary contribution is application to converged models which is incremental

Weak theoretical justification for why interpositional growth preserves functionality better than stacking: argument relies on empirical correlation of norm distributions without establishing causality or mechanistic understanding
MoE-specific scope significantly limits generalizability: applicability to dense models not explored, reducing relevance for broader ML community
Narrow evaluation scope limited to knowledge/QA benchmarks (MMLU + 6 tasks): no generation quality evaluation, no downstream task finetuning, no evaluation on language modeling diversity

Questionable fairness of main comparison to scratch training: Figure 1/abstract emphasize 10.66% improvement with 'same additional compute' but compare different initialization points; Figure 8 with fixed total FLOPs shows much smaller improvements but is underemphasized

Incomplete analysis of key design choices: noise injection parameter α=0.01 appears optimal but single value tested on one model/dataset; 1% improvement from noise is modest with no statistical significance testing; limited exploration of width vs. depth selection criteria

Limited baseline comparisons: only compares against scratch training and stacking method; does not directly compare against other contemporary growth methods (LEMON, LiGO, etc.) mentioned in related work

Missing mechanistic understanding of correlation between sunk cost and performance: unclear whether benefit is from growth method itself or simply from better initialization; alternative explanations not addressed
Scalability validation limited to 70B parameters: unclear if approach scales to 100B+ parameter models or frontier scales; single scale-up trajectory (17B→35B→70B) is one data point

strengths: Comprehensive large-scale experiments spanning 3B to 70B parameters with 1T tokens, demonstrating genuine scalability and practical relevance
Novel empirical insight linking layer-wise weight norm patterns to model convergence state, with principled connection to neural ODE regularization theory

Thorough orthogonality analysis across multiple perspectives (structural disjointness, gradient direction, weight update divergence, order independence) providing strong evidence for compositional growth
Extensive reproducibility documentation including architectural specifications, dataset composition, hyperparameters, and infrastructure details enabling verification and reproduction
Systematic ablations on growth factor k, noise levels, routing variants, and growth timing with clear presentation of trade-offs and design choices
Practical methodology with clear guidelines for when interposition outperforms stacking (well-converged models >1× Chinchilla-optimal FLOPs)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—layer duplication and expert initialization are well-established techniques; the interposition insight, while useful, is an incremental refinement of prior stacking approaches

Efficiency claims overstated: the prominent 10.6% improvement compares different model sizes (70B vs 17B); in realistic fixed-total-budget scenarios (Figure 10), advantages are modest (2-3%) or absent, undermining the core efficiency narrative
Incomplete baseline comparisons—no direct comparison to LLaMA Pro, other recent growth methods, or alternative efficient scaling approaches; scratch-trained baseline is underspecified

Scope limitations: insights specific to MoE architectures with unclear generalization to dense models; evaluation limited to multiple-choice QA and MMLU without generation quality metrics or human evaluation

Weight norm preservation justified empirically but lacks deep theoretical explanation; unclear why this specific structural property should be prioritized or how universal this principle is across architectures and datasets

Sunk-cost framing potentially misleading—efficiency gains depend on pre-trained checkpoints already existing; for many real-world scenarios (new orgs, new architectures), this assumption doesn't hold, limiting practical applicability
